# Electrical faults, grounds and battery drain

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Connect a scan tool to the ABS system then navigate the menu to select an ABS function. [t18]

[Partial] Inspect negative battery terminal connection, replace if necessary, check fusible links, and consult FSM for ground locations. [t19]

[Partial] Find a bolt or nut on the vehicle body to use as a ground point. [t11]

Locate the fuse and relay box under the hood next to the windshield washer bottle, then check the blower motor relay. [t7]

[Partial] Pop off drink holder molding and identify yaw sensor plug with four wires. [t753]

[Partial] Check the fuse box, verify 30A shared fuses, and inspect brown relays behind the passenger front kick panel. [t269]

Switch the vehicle into 4WD mode then drive forward. [t517]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Pop off the drink holder molding located at the back near the center console.
2. Identify the yaw sensor plug with four wires (brown, white, cream, and yellow).
3. [Partial] Unplug the yaw sensor connector to disable the ABS system.
4. [Partial] If using a switch instead of unplugging, pull the brown ground wire out from the wiring harness.
5. [Partial] Snip the brown wire in half to separate it into two ends.
6. [Partial] Connect both cut ends of the brown wire to an electrical switch.
7. To use a rocker push switch with lighting, install a 5 pin relay.
8. Wire terminal 86 on the relay to the signal wire from the ABS Off switch.
9. Wire terminal 85 on the relay to ground.
10. Connect terminal 30 on the relay to the front section of the brown ground wire in the harness.
11. Connect terminal 87a on the relay to the rear section of the brown ground wire in the harness.
12. Leave terminal 87 unconnected for this specific setup.

_Procedure reported by [t753]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-abs-off-mod.9070/>_

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t11] [Partial]</summary>

1. Find a bolt or nut on the vehicle body to use as a ground point.
2. Remove the fastener and sand down the area until bare metal is exposed.
3. Attach the grounding wire securely, then replace the nut/bolt.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t7] [Partial]</summary>

1. Locate the fuse and relay box under the hood next to the windshield washer bottle.
2. Check the blower motor relay within that box.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t517] [Partial]</summary>

1. Switch the vehicle into 4WD mode.
2. Drive forward for a few feet.

</details>

## Tips & gotchas

- Check fusible links on the positive cable side as an alternative power source issue. [t19]
- Consult the Factory Service Manual (FSM) for specific ground locations, starting with body and chassis grounds. [t19]
- Consult the PG chapter of a service manual for an electrical units location section if needed. [t7]
- [Partial] Swap in a known good brown relay from another slot to test functionality. [t7]
- The brown wire serves as the ground for the plug. [t753]
- A momentary switch will interrupt ABS and keep it off until an engine restart. [t753]
- Use a 5-pin relay where pin 86 connects to the ABS Off switch signal. [t753]
- Connect pin 85 to ground and pin 30 to the front portion of the brown wire from the harness. [t753]
- [Partial] The 30-87a connection is normally on, while the signal triggers the switch to move it to 30-87. [t753]
- [Partial] Inspect relays located behind the passenger front kick panel, especially when using an OE-style 7-pin connector. [t269]
- Ensure specific brown relays are functioning correctly as they may supply constant power. [t269]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Assuming all fuses under the hood are fine without checking for a dedicated constant power fuse specifically. [t269]
